Explanation: A completed ride is the core value unit: a rider requests transport, DiDi matches the request with available local supply, and a driver provides the trip.
DiDi owns and operates the mobility platform, manages matching and payments, sets platform rules, and builds services that help riders and drivers transact.
DiDi has to make sure enough drivers are available in each local market when riders request trips.
DiDi benefits when more trips are completed and the platform keeps a share of transaction value after driver and partner earnings, incentives, tolls, fees and taxes.
The marketplace becomes less useful when too few drivers are available, and DiDi must operate within transport, safety, labor and data rules across many markets.
DiDi coordinates trip requests, matching and payment. Its reported Platform Sales measure is transaction value after driver and partner earnings and other deductions.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Request / Pay — The rider asks DiDi for a trip and pays through the platform or a supported method. | → Provider · Offer — DiDi sends a trip opportunity to an eligible nearby driver based on location and marketplace conditions. | → Consumer · Match / ETA — DiDi shows the rider the matched driver, pickup information and expected arrival details. | → Provider · Payout — DiDi coordinates payment and driver earnings after completed trips.

Explanation: DiDi sets and enforces rules for driver eligibility, vehicles, safety, service quality, pricing and dispute handling while adapting to local regulation.
Riders access DiDi through its apps and, in China, also through mini-programs in services such as WeChat and Alipay.
DiDi predicts supply and demand, matches riders and drivers, routes trips, processes payments, supports users and manages safety and service quality.
Important resources include rider demand, driver supply, trip and location data, mapping, matching technology, AI systems and the DiDi brand.
People use DiDi when they need an on-demand trip or another mobility service.
Riders want to arrange transport quickly without having to find and negotiate with a driver themselves.
DiDi can give riders several mobility options, estimated arrival information and a simple digital booking and payment process.
Riders can face long waits when supply is scarce, changing prices, cancellations or safety concerns.
The rider enters a destination, requests a trip and pays through the platform or a supported payment method.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Request / Pay — The rider asks DiDi for a trip and pays through the platform or a supported method. | ← Owner · Match / ETA — DiDi shows the rider the matched driver, pickup information and expected arrival details. | ← Provider · Ride — The driver provides the physical transport from pickup to destination.

Explanation: A trip can only be matched where DiDi operates and where suitable local driver supply is available.
Consumers can access DiDi through its mobile apps and, in China, through mini-programs on apps such as WeChat and Alipay.
Riders request a trip, meet the driver, take the ride, pay and can provide feedback about the experience.
Riders bring trip demand, pickup and destination information, payment data and ratings that help the marketplace operate.
Drivers provide the physical transport service using their time and access to an eligible vehicle.
Drivers want a steady source of nearby trip demand that can turn available driving time into income.
DiDi can provide ride demand and can also reduce barriers through vehicle leasing, fuel discounts and charging access.
Drivers need an affordable vehicle and face fuel or charging costs, maintenance costs and unpaid time between trips.
Drivers receive trip opportunities, choose whether to accept them and complete the physical ride.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Offer — DiDi sends a trip opportunity to an eligible nearby driver based on location and marketplace conditions. | → Consumer · Ride — The driver provides the physical transport from pickup to destination. | ← Owner · Payout — DiDi coordinates payment and driver earnings after completed trips. | ← Partner · Car / Charge — Vehicle and energy partners help drivers access cars, leasing, charging or fuel so they can stay active on the platform.

Explanation: Drivers and vehicles must meet DiDi requirements and applicable local legal and safety rules before providing rides.
Drivers use DiDi's driver tools to go online, receive trip requests and manage work on the platform.
Drivers make themselves available, accept suitable trips, transport riders and keep vehicles and documents in working order.
Drivers contribute their time, driving ability, local knowledge, required licenses and access to a suitable vehicle.
Leasing companies, financial institutions, charging operators and other vehicle-service partners help drivers get vehicles and keep them operating.
Partners make vehicles, leasing, financing, charging and related services available so more drivers can participate in ride-hailing.
Partners gain access to a very large base of high-mileage drivers who need vehicles, energy and ongoing automotive services.
Vehicle and energy partners need enough driver demand to justify assets and infrastructure while meeting financial, transport and energy rules.
Partners provide vehicles, charging, refuelling or financing that helps drivers stay active on the marketplace.
Transaction Flows: → Provider · Car / Charge — Vehicle and energy partners help drivers access cars, leasing, charging or fuel so they can stay active on the platform.

Explanation: Partners must meet DiDi and local requirements and have useful geographic coverage for drivers.
DiDi connects drivers to leasing, refuelling and charging services through its energy and vehicle service ecosystem.
Partners provide vehicles, financing, charging or fuel access and keep the underlying assets and services available.
Partners contribute vehicles, charging stations, fuel networks, financing capacity and automotive operating expertise.
